Which implementation and control?

MethodOriginal 1DAuthor-code comparison
Weight repulsionOur parameter-space KDE regularizerReleased D’Angelo KDE-WGD update with a Gaussian weight prior
Functional repulsionOur output-space KDE regularizerReleased functional KDE-WGD with an SSGE function-prior force
FoRDEOur normalized-gradient repulsionReleased FoRDE repulsion function inside our scalar-regression adapter
No-repulsion baselineOriginal DEAuthor baseline for weight KDE-WGD; FoRDE matched control for the JAX FoRDE adapter

The released D’Angelo scalar code has a network-count factor in its driving gradient; the JAX FoRDE adapter does not. Functional KDE-WGD also changes the prior representation. A comparison across these methods therefore changes more than the repulsion term. The FoRDE matched control preserves its adapter and removes only repulsion. BDKN and the FoRDE regression combination are our extensions.

Settings and downloads

D’Angelo paper training recipe: 50 networks, 2 × 50 ReLU, Adam LR 0.01, 15,000 gradient steps, batch size 64, seed 42; standard Gaussian likelihood and N(0,I) prior. Existing datasets are kept fixed. On author x sin x, the released generator uses noise standard deviation 0.25; the paper’s Gaussian variance notation is ambiguous relative to that code. Other datasets transfer this training recipe. FoRDE and BDKN are extensions.

Upstream implementation

Pinned author source · 6dcb4c068082

  • data/dataset.py: np.int replaced with built-in int (same integer dtype)
  • methods/method_utils.py: f_SVGD resolved to methods/f_SVGD.py
  • utils/SSGE_squeeze.py: symmetric torch.eig replaced by torch.linalg.eigh; all eigenpairs retained, no clipping
  • methods/SVGD.py: remove broken duplicate SGD.step; retain first upstream SGD.step verbatim

Our-settings runs change architecture, input preprocessing, learning rate and update budget. The upstream scalar head, fixed-noise likelihood, prior and update rule are retained. BDKN extensions are ours.

Author updates

Author baseline

\ell(\theta)=\log p(\theta)-\frac{N}{2B\sigma^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B}(y_b-f_\theta(x_b))^2,\qquad g_i=-H\nabla_{\theta_i}\ell(\theta_i)

Author weight-space KDE-WGD

g_i=-H\nabla_{\theta_i}\ell(\theta_i)+\frac{\sum_j\nabla_{\theta_i}k(\theta_i,\operatorname{sg}(\theta_j))}{\sum_jk(\theta_i,\operatorname{sg}(\theta_j))}

Author functional KDE-WGD

g_i=-J_i^\top\left[H\nabla_{f_i}\log p(y\mid f_i)+\widehat{\nabla_{f_i}\log p(f_i)}_{\mathrm{SSGE}}-\frac{\sum_j\nabla_{f_i}k(f_i,\operatorname{sg}(f_j))}{\sum_jk(f_i,\operatorname{sg}(f_j))}\right]

Shared kernel

k(z_i,z_j)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\lVert z_i-z_j\rVert^2}{2s^2}\right),\qquad s^2=\operatorname{sg}\!\left(\frac{\operatorname{median}_{i,j}\lVert z_i-z_j\rVert^2}{2\log(H+1)}\right)

gᵢ: gradient passed to Adam; θᵢ: network parameters; N: training count; B: batch size; H: network count; σ: fixed likelihood standard deviation (1); fᵢ: network outputs on the shared batch; Jᵢ: parameter Jacobian; zᵢ: parameters for weight-space repulsion or outputs for functional repulsion; s²: kernel bandwidth; sg: stop-gradient. Self pairs are included. Functional prior scores use SSGE with regularization 0.01.

Released-code driving scale

For scalar regression the pinned D’Angelo code broadcasts a likelihood tensor of shape H × 1 with a parameter-prior tensor of shape H. Its summed posterior therefore multiplies likelihood/prior driving gradients by H, as shown above; the independent author ensemble has the same factor. This released behavior is retained. The FoRDE hybrid and its matched JAX control use the direct scalar objective D + P, without that broadcasting factor. Compare the hybrid with its JAX control to isolate repulsion.

D’Angelo regression setup + author FoRDE repulsion

Pinned FoRDE JAX source · e8f9d7418be4. The released FoRDE experiments classify images. This combination retains D’Angelo’s scalar regression model, fixed Gaussian noise (std 1), N(0,I) parameter prior, actual initial parameter arrays, shared batch stream and Adam settings. Only the diversity term is replaced by the original FoRDE repulsion function. Its PCA geometry is fitted on training inputs only. This is a regression combination, not a published FoRDE regression experiment.

u_{ib}=\frac{g_{ib}V}{\sqrt{\lVert g_{ib}V\rVert^2+\epsilon}}\odot s,\quad d_{ijb}=\lVert u_{ib}-\operatorname{sg}(u_{jb})\rVert^2,\quad h_{jb}=\frac{\operatorname{median}_{i}\operatorname{sg}(d_{ijb})}{\log H}+10^{-12}
R=\frac1B\sum_i\left[\operatorname{LSE}_{j,b}\!\left(-\frac{d_{ijb}}{h_{jb}}\right)-\log B\right],\quad L=\frac{N}{2B}\sum_{i,b}(y_b-\mu_i(x_b))^2+\frac12\lVert\Theta\rVert^2+R+\mathrm{const}

g: mean-input derivative; V: training PCA directions; s: square-root PCA eigenvalues; ε = 10⁻²⁴; H: networks; N: training count; B: batch size; LSE: log-sum-exp. The control sets R to zero and shares initial parameters, batches, prior and Adam settings. In one dimension normalization can leave almost only derivative signs; zero or tiny repulsive parameter gradients are retained and plotted.

Upstream preset: D’Angelo README configuration (100 networks, 10×10 hidden units, LR 0.01, 5,000 steps). Low/high: 5 networks, 50×50 units, LR 0.001/0.1, update counts matching 2,000/40 training passes. All use Adam (0.9, 0.999, ε = 10⁻⁸). BDKN is our separate frozen-network extension. Timings include first-use JAX compilation.
